# Reconstruct a triangular mesh from a 3D point cloud

Reconstructs a triangular surface from a 3D point cloud using linear
binning and Marching Cubes, and returns the result as a `mesh3d` object.

## Usage

``` r
createMesh(
  cloud,
  resolNbin = c(4, 4, 2),
  meshCad = NULL,
  zeroBorder = FALSE,
  kFactor = NULL,
  truncFactor = 3.5,
  levelFactor = 0.99,
  coverageTol = 0.99
)
```

## Arguments

- cloud:

  Numeric matrix or data frame with three columns containing the X, Y,
  and Z coordinates of the point cloud.

- resolNbin:

  Numeric vector of length three defining the approximate binning
  resolution in the X, Y, and Z directions. Default is `c(4, 4, 2)`.

- meshCad:

  `mesh3d` object used as a reference for the spatial coverage of the
  reconstructed surface. Default is `NULL`, in which case the dimensions
  of the point cloud are used.

- zeroBorder:

  Logical. If `TRUE`, adds a zero-valued layer around the X and Z limits
  before surface extraction. Default is `FALSE`.

- kFactor:

  Numeric value used to determine the tolerance for removing low-density
  nodes. If `NULL`, it is selected automatically according to
  `resolNbin`. Default is `NULL`.

- truncFactor:

  Numeric value used to truncate high-density node weights. Default is
  `3.5`.

- levelFactor:

  Numeric value used to define the isosurface extraction level. Default
  is `0.99`.

- coverageTol:

  Numeric value between 0 and 1 defining the minimum spatial coverage
  required relative to the reference dimensions. Default is `0.99`.

## Value

List containing:

- `mesh`: `mesh3d` object containing the reconstructed triangular
  surface.

- `bin`: processed binning object used for surface reconstruction.

- `contours`: list of disconnected surfaces generated by Marching Cubes,
  ordered from largest to smallest according to their number of
  triangles.

- `params`: list containing the parameters used during reconstruction.

## Details

Linear binning is performed using
[`npsp::binning()`](http://rubenfcasal.github.io/npsp/reference/binning.md),
and the corresponding grid coordinates are obtained with
[`npsp::coordvalues()`](http://rubenfcasal.github.io/npsp/reference/coordvalues.md).
Low-density nodes are removed and high-density weights are truncated
before extracting the isosurface with
[`misc3d::contour3d()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/misc3d/man/contour3d.html).

When `zeroBorder = TRUE`, one zero-valued layer is added on both sides
of the X and Z directions to facilitate surface closure.

If several disconnected surfaces are generated, they are ordered by
number of triangles and progressively merged. Components are added until
the dimensions of the reconstructed surface reach at least `coverageTol`
times the reference dimensions. If `meshCad = NULL`, the point-cloud
dimensions are used as the reference; otherwise, the dimensions of
`meshCad` are used.

The resulting surface is converted to a triangular `mesh3d` object using
[`rgl::tmesh3d()`](https://dmurdoch.github.io/rgl/dev/reference/mesh3d.html).

## See also

[`npsp::binning()`](http://rubenfcasal.github.io/npsp/reference/binning.md),
[`npsp::coordvalues()`](http://rubenfcasal.github.io/npsp/reference/coordvalues.md),
[`misc3d::contour3d()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/misc3d/man/contour3d.html),
[`rgl::tmesh3d()`](https://dmurdoch.github.io/rgl/dev/reference/mesh3d.html)

## Examples

``` r
library(rgl)

# Load the theoretical CAD model
data("cad", package = "dimControl")

# Simulate object points without floor points
object <- simulateCloud(mesh = cad, n = 1e5)

# Reconstruct the mesh from the object point cloud
result <- createMesh(cloud = object, resolNbin = c(12, 12, 6), zeroBorder = TRUE,
                     kFactor = 0.01, truncFactor = 1.5, levelFactor = 0.99)

# Represent point cloud and reconstructed mesh side by side
# open3d() # Alternatively, use `legendplot::new3d()` to clear the current device or open a new one
 mfrow3d(1, 2)

 points3d(object, col = "blue")
 title3d("object point cloud", line = 8, level = 2)

 next3d()
 shade3d(result$mesh, col = "lightgray")
 title3d("Reconstructed mesh", line = 8, level = 2)
```
